Timestral as a fable model

Source: R/fable.R
TIMESTRAL.Rd

Defines a Timestral zero-shot forecasting model for use with fabletools::model() on a tsibble. The response is univariate (use timestral_forecast() directly for jointly forecast multiple variates); keys in the tsibble are handled by fable as usual, with the model trained (context captured) independently per key. Requires the fabletools package (and fable for the usual workflow); forecasts are reported as 21-quantile distributions.

Usage

TIMESTRAL(formula, model, symmetric = TRUE, clip_nonnegative = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

formula

the response formula, as in other fable models, e.g. TIMESTRAL(value)

model

a timestral_model from timestral_load(); loaded once and reused for every key and forecast. Fitted models store only the checkpoint directory and load settings, not the weights, so a mable stays small when saved and is reloaded from disk when forecast in a new R session or a parallel worker.

symmetric, clip_nonnegative

as in timestral_forecast()

...

passed to the model definition (currently unused)

Value

a fable model definition, for use inside fabletools::model()

Examples

## the tiny bundled checkpoint runs offline but its forecasts are
## meaningless; use timestral_load("5M") or larger for real ones
m <- timestral_load(system.file("extdata", "tiny", package = "timestralR"))
if (requireNamespace("fable", quietly = TRUE)) {
  fit <- tsibble::as_tsibble(AirPassengers) |>
    fabletools::model(timestral = TIMESTRAL(value, model = m))
  fit |> fabletools::forecast(h = 24)
}
#> # A fable: 24 x 4 [1M]
#> # Key:     .model [1]

#>    <chr>        <mth>       <dist> <dbl>

#>  3 timestral 1961 Mar quantile[21]  283.
#>  4 timestral 1961 Apr quantile[21]  314.
#>  5 timestral 1961 May quantile[21]  206.
#>  6 timestral 1961 Jun quantile[21]  177.
#>  7 timestral 1961 Jul quantile[21]  360.
#>  8 timestral 1961 Aug quantile[21]  245.
#>  9 timestral 1961 Sep quantile[21]  269.
#> 10 timestral 1961 Oct quantile[21]  316.
